title: Describe deforming motifs by their responses, not their silhouettes

sources.use: Borrow simulation illumination through behavioral representations.
sources.boundary: Representation diversity does not establish physical function.

sources.use: Borrow graph paths as explicit mechanism suggestions.
sources.boundary: Semantic edges do not supply mechanical constants.

mechanism: Propose positive-stiffness spring motifs. A connectivity-to-deformation graph path selects displacement under two loads as a descriptor. Geometric neighbors become springs, with forces derived from quadratic energy. Archives compare measured responses instead of silhouettes; graph edges never supply mechanical constants.
hypothesis: Response descriptors may distinguish visually similar motifs with different load transfer, while visual descriptors may separate silhouettes that implement nearly identical responses.
experiment: On CPU, sample 100 twelve-node motifs and solve fixed-boundary linear equilibria. Build equal-size response and silhouette archives from the identical pool; evaluate withheld load directions.
baseline: Match motif pools, archive sizes and equilibrium solves for response, silhouette and random archives.
metric: Report pairwise distances between held-out displacement responses and reconstruction of response classes, alongside occupied bins under a fixed independent evaluator.
falsifier: Reject the proposed advantage if held-out response separation is no better than random across repeated pools, or follows only node count or stiffness totals.
confound: Unconstrained rigid modes and overall stiffness can dominate distances; fix boundaries, normalize material budget and report dimensional versus normalized responses.
feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

title: Compile relation graphs into a bounded Lenia kernel grammar

sources.use: Borrow niche archives of continuous cellular patterns.
sources.boundary: This toy does not demonstrate open-ended evolution.

sources.use: Borrow interpretable relational representations for candidate construction.
sources.boundary: Conceptual relations do not determine kernel physics.

mechanism: Propose a graph grammar for continuous cellular automata. Nodes denote channels; edges compile to normalized radial kernels and bounded growth coefficients. An inhibition relation proposes an edge type, with mathematics independently defined. Compare graph mutations against flat coefficient mutations.
hypothesis: If reusable motifs provide useful search structure, grammar mutations may retain viable patterns more often than matched flat mutations after a new channel coupling is introduced.
experiment: Run 60 paired mutations on a 32-by-32 grid for 150 steps, matching starting patterns and parameter ranges; evaluate a withheld seed.
baseline: Match coefficient counts, mutation norms, rollouts and archive capacities; add a label-shuffled grammar.
metric: Measure surviving localized patterns after mutation and held-out-seed persistence; report descriptor coverage using one frozen evaluator for every encoding.
falsifier: Reject a grammar benefit if matched flat encoding performs equally or better, or any apparent gain disappears after matching the distribution of coefficient changes.
confound: Grammar search may silently restrict candidates to safer regions. Log the induced parameter distribution and compare conditioned subsets before attributing a compositional advantage.
feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

title: Test when nonreciprocal particle couplings produce functional pursuit

sources.use: Borrow typed-particle interaction matrices as a searchable substrate.
sources.boundary: Attraction patterns alone do not establish agency.

sources.use: Borrow paths to propose testable directional relationships.
sources.boundary: A graph arrow is not evidence for a force law.

mechanism: Propose a two-species overdamped particle toy where a graph path suggests asymmetric sensing. Specify bounded radial interactions a12 and a21; drag removes momentum conservation. Search reciprocal and nonreciprocal families for localized pursuit tracking a displaced resource, rather than task-free circling.
hypothesis: Under specified drag and resource attraction, asymmetric coefficients may support sustained pursuit with better tracking than reciprocal couplings of the same interaction strength.
experiment: Simulate 24 particles for 400 steps over 40 coefficient pairs and ten seeds; displace a resource halfway through and measure tracking after the intervention.
baseline: Match force bounds, drag, seeds and rollouts for reciprocal, asymmetric and species-shuffled controls.
metric: Use post-displacement resource distance, cluster persistence and speed; include total force magnitude to expose gains purchased by stronger actuation.
falsifier: Reject the pursuit claim if tracking gains vanish under matched force magnitude or occur equally when the resource displacement signal is removed.
confound: Circular motion can masquerade as tracking, and boundary wrapping can reduce apparent distances; use unwrapped trajectories and counterfactual resource positions.
feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

title: Couple elastic deformation to a local reaction pattern

sources.use: Borrow persistence and locomotion measures for local patterns.
sources.boundary: A reaction toy is not a Lenia replication.

sources.use: Borrow explicit graph interpretation linked to executable modeling.
sources.boundary: Retrieved analogies do not establish constitutive equations.

mechanism: Propose an elastic ring carrying an activator-inhibitor field. A strain-to-activation-to-rest-length cycle compiles to explicit equations: strain adds bounded activation, activation changes rest lengths, and positions follow elastic gradients. Declare external chemical drive; graph relations supply dependencies, never unvalidated material constants.
hypothesis: Within a stable parameter region, two-way coupling may preserve a traveling excitation after a localized mechanical disturbance more often than one-way coupling.
experiment: Sweep 30 coupling settings, ten seeds and 500 steps; indent one ring node at a fixed time and track pulse propagation and recovery with timestep-halving checks.
baseline: Match initial fields, elastic budgets and integration calls across two-way, one-way and zero coupling.
metric: Measure pulse lap completion, recovery time and bounded deformation; report chemical drive and elastic dissipation separately rather than inferring efficiency.
falsifier: Reject the coupling advantage if it disappears under timestep refinement or if comparable persistence requires no strain feedback.
confound: Numerical instability and imposed reaction oscillations can mimic self-organization; test isolated field dynamics, boundedness and dependence on initial phase.
feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

title: Give a spring motif a local record of previous loading

sources.use: Borrow trajectory-conditioned searches for dynamical motifs.
sources.boundary: Distinct trajectories do not establish useful memory.

sources.use: Borrow executable constitutive fitting and validation loops.
sources.boundary: The proposed law is not an experimentally fitted material.

mechanism: Propose spring motifs with slow rest-length variables relaxing toward extension. A loading-history-response path maps to an explicit internal-variable energy with positive relaxation and damping. Search relaxation times for history discrimination while matching geometry and current force; graph analogy establishes no constitutive validity.
hypothesis: A slow internal variable may preserve information about pulse order after fast displacement relaxes, permitting better discrimination than a memoryless spring motif.
experiment: Apply AB and BA load pulses with equal total impulse; after a fixed delay, apply the same probe and classify histories using displacement in 100 noisy repeats.
baseline: Use frozen-memory and randomized-history controls; match geometry, stiffness, pulse energy and classifier data.
metric: Report held-out history classification, decay with delay and dissipated work; test whether separation survives conditioning on the visible pre-probe geometry.
falsifier: Reject hidden-memory behavior if classification falls to chance after geometry matching, or if initial-state leakage predicts history equally well.
confound: Residual displacement, unequal work and classifier overfitting can mimic memory; split by noisy realization and audit the full mechanical state before probing.
feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

title: Separate refractory-state memory from visible cellular shape

sources.use: Borrow phenotype trajectories and localized-pattern evaluation.
sources.boundary: A latent descriptor does not identify causal memory.

sources.use: Borrow a graph path to formulate a mechanistic hypothesis.
sources.boundary: The graph supplies an experimental suggestion, not proof.

mechanism: Propose a cellular pattern with refractory channel h integrating activation and inhibiting growth. The activation-to-refractoriness-to-response path maps to h-next=(1-alpha)h+alpha*x plus inhibited growth. Swap or reset h while keeping visible x identical to causally test state-dependent responses rather than infer memory from descriptors.
hypothesis: If refractory state stores operational history, identical visible patterns should respond differently to an identical probe after h swapping, with differences decaying at the specified relaxation timescale.
experiment: Use 32-by-32 grids, paired activation pulses and ten seeds; copy visible state across matched histories, then swap hidden channels before applying a fixed probe.
baseline: Use reset-memory, shuffled-memory and memoryless controls; match grids, rollouts, patterns and probes.
metric: Measure probe-induced mass change and recovery latency as functions of pulse interval; estimate the causal effect of hidden-channel replacement on matched visible states.
falsifier: Reject a refractory-memory explanation if hidden-state swaps do not alter response, or differences persist unchanged after resetting h.
confound: A hidden channel can simply change effective excitability. Compare spatially shuffled and constant-mean h to distinguish local history structure from a scalar gain change.
feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

title: Select locally persistent patterns for recovery across lesion types

sources.use: Borrow local competition in a behavioral archive.
sources.boundary: Archive occupancy does not prove biological adaptability.

sources.use: Borrow structure-function paths to propose intervention families.
sources.boundary: Materials analogies do not certify cellular regeneration.

mechanism: Propose selecting cellular patterns in mass-speed niches, replacing persistence fitness with lesion recovery. A redundancy-to-connectivity-to-damage-tolerance path proposes central and peripheral erasure. These operators act on cellular state; graph terminology changes no growth equations and asserts no tissue equivalence.
hypothesis: At equal rollout budget, lesion-conditioned selection may improve recovery to withheld lesion locations compared with selection for undisturbed persistence alone.
experiment: Mutate 80 candidates around a known viable seed on a 32-by-32 grid. Alternate two training lesion classes; evaluate retained patterns on held-out wedge lesions and seeds.
baseline: Match mutations, niches and simulation steps; give persistence-only selection extra repeated evaluations.
metric: Measure post-lesion survival, normalized mass recovery and connected-pattern retention; report undisturbed persistence and occupied niches to expose robustness-diversity tradeoffs.
falsifier: Reject transferable recovery if gains occur only for trained lesion masks, reflect simply larger initial mass, or disappear on held-out initial conditions.
confound: Mass and empty-space placement can mechanically reduce lesion severity; match fractional mass removed and analyze size-stratified outcomes.
feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.

title: Select visual novelty against intervention-tested function

sources.use: Borrow historical novelty and representation-based illumination.
sources.boundary: A novelty proxy does not establish functional innovation.

sources.use: Borrow interpretable hypotheses checked by executable modeling.
sources.boundary: Graph assertions require an independently specified test.

mechanism: Propose excitable cellular motifs where graph paths name functions compiled into perturbation assays. Compare visual novelty selection against response novelty conditional on viability. A control renderer adds color cycles without changing state; functional responses are measured on unrendered dynamics, not semantic descriptions.
hypothesis: Function-conditioned selection may resist color-cycle novelty traps better than visual selection while retaining patterns with distinct responses to local deletion and timed excitation.
experiment: Evaluate 80 shared candidate rules on 24-by-24 grids with three renderers; build equal-capacity archives and evaluate unselected perturbation times and deletion locations.
baseline: Match pools, rollouts, assays and archive sizes for visual, response and random selection; count descriptor costs.
metric: Report renderer sensitivity of archive membership, held-out response diversity and viable fraction; compute function descriptors using fixed lesion and excitation definitions.
falsifier: Reject the selection advantage if response-selected archives lack more held-out functional diversity than random or are equally altered by renderer-only changes.
confound: Handcrafted assays privilege chosen functions and may miss meaningful visual dynamics; preserve disagreements rather than declaring visual novelty scientifically worthless.
feasibility: One-day dimensionless CPU toy using NumPy; physical validation, biological agency and open-ended evolution remain unestablished.
